grammar_focus: Wh-nominal clauses functioning as the subject of a cleft-style sentence
explanation: A wh-nominal clause such as 'what puzzled the investigators most' works as a noun phrase, so the verb that follows must express what the clause identifies. The contrast 'not ... but' then names the real focus of the puzzle.
